name: AlgebraicSpaces
scope: This roadmap develops the Grothendieck topologies on schemes and the descent theory they support, and builds algebraic spaces on them. It covers the Zariski, étale, smooth, fppf and fpqc topologies and the v- and arc-topologies, effective fpqc descent for quasi-coherent sheaves and affine morphisms, descent of properties of morphisms, torsors under flat group schemes, and Čech and flat cohomology, with H¹_fppf(Spec k, μ_n) = k^×/k^{×n} and Grothendieck's comparison of fppf and étale cohomology for smooth commutative group schemes. Algebraic spaces are fppf sheaves with representable diagonal and an étale atlas; the roadmap develops their morphisms and properties, fibre products, quotients by étale equivalence relations and by free actions of finite groups, Weil restriction, and Artin's representability criterion with its hypotheses. It consumes Mathlib's fpqc and étale sites, ModularCurves Layer 0E's effective descent and ReductiveGroups' fppf quotients rather than rebuilding them. Étale cohomology with torsion coefficients belongs to CohomologicalPointCounting; stacks belong to AlgebraicStacks.

name: HilbertQuotAndPicardSchemes
scope: This roadmap constructs the projective parameter spaces of algebraic geometry. It starts with projective, Grassmann and flag bundles of locally free sheaves and their tautological bundles, Castelnuovo–Mumford regularity and flattening stratifications (the first successor named by AlgebraicVectorBundles), and proves Grothendieck's representability of Hilbert and Quot functors of projective schemes over a Noetherian base, with Hom schemes and Hilbert schemes of points (Fogarty's smoothness for surfaces). It then builds the relative Picard functor and its representability for projective flat X/S with geometrically integral fibres, Pic⁰ and Pic^τ, the tangent space H¹(X, O_X) and smoothness in characteristic zero, and the Néron–Severi group with the theorem of the base, compared with AbundanceStatement's numerical group. Formal deformation theory closes it: Schlessinger's criterion, tangent–obstruction theories of Hilbert, Quot and Hom functors, Grothendieck existence and Artin algebraization. JacobianChallenge's rigidified Picard functor of curves is specialized, not redefined; moduli stacks are AlgebraicStacks.
